description: Source-lore pass 20 imports criminal status and law enforcement, chase and escape roles, marooned-island survival, and minor-island encounter and contents tables.

entries.title: Law Enforcement and Criminal Status
entries.summary: Kaysender law is enforced by city guards, elite Watchers, specialized Enforcers, courts, and guild tribunals, while criminal status escalates from accusation to bounty, outlawry, conviction, or attempted redemption.
body: City Guards handle urban order, theft, tavern violence, and ordinary crime. Elite Watchers investigate major, political, or covert offenses. Enforcers include bounty hunters, interrogators, and specialists who locate fugitives and carry out punishment.

Courts use judges, barristers, sentencing, appeal, and formal legal proceedings. Guilds also maintain internal law, imposing fines, expulsion, blacklisting, or assassination orders for extreme violations.

An accused person awaits trial and may seek counsel, influence, escape, or a negotiated sentence. A wanted criminal carries a bounty and attracts guards, informants, and hunters. An outlaw may lose ordinary trial protections and face immediate punishment. A convicted criminal must serve fines, imprisonment, forced labor, or worse unless they escape or earn relief.

Bribery can soften enforcement but invites escalating corruption and exposure. Nobles, guilds, and political patrons may alter cases, while secret routes and false documents help fugitives leave a jurisdiction without erasing the underlying crime.
Redemption may require public service, recovery of stolen property, solving crimes, informing on dangerous groups, or proving loyalty to authorities. Offers of amnesty can themselves be traps.

sections.heading: Legacy Crime Economy
body: The source suggests bribe ranges from modest sums for minor offenses to hundreds or thousands of gold for serious crimes. These values require conversion.

entries.title: Escape and Pursuit
entries.summary: Dramatic escapes combine initiative, route choice, stealth, speed, evasion, distraction, obstruction, endurance, coordination, disengagement, hazards, and occasional last stands.
body: Escape begins with acting before pursuers can close the gap. The fleeing group chooses terrain, streets, crowds, currents, clouds, or open sky that create distance without leading into traps or dead ends.
On foot, stealth and endurance matter alongside raw speed. Escapees hide, blend into crowds, sprint, climb, dodge attacks, block paths, create distractions, and resist exhaustion.

Aboard a ship, pilots exploit wind and terrain while the crew coordinates engines, sails, repairs, cargo, and defensive action. Disengagement breaks a vessel out of combat; failed coordination lets pursuers close or forces a prolonged fight.

Environmental hazards threaten both sides. Storms, creatures, unstable ground, obstacles, and magical effects may provide cover or become new dangers. A final stand can buy time for others but risks capture, injury, or death.
Successful escape is usually cumulative: several people perform complementary roles rather than relying on one speed check.

sections.heading: Legacy Chase Roles
body: The source provides thirteen roles with DC ranges and outcomes for initiative, terrain, stealth, foot and ship speed, evasion, distraction, obstruction, perseverance, coordination, disengagement, final stands, and hazards. Conversion is required.

entries.title: Marooned on a Minor Sky Island
entries.summary: A stranded traveler survives by scouting, securing water, predicting weather, signaling ships, attracting creatures, and constructing crude gliders, rafts, lights, flags, rockets, or beacons.
body: Minor sky islands are often less than one hundred fifty feet across and drift readily with the wind. A stranded person must first survey resources, high ground, visibility, shelter, weather, food, and [[water-in-the-skies|water]].

Rescue signals can use smoke, night fires, flags, reflective scraps, drums, horns, glowstones, torches, rockets, and large stone or timber beacons. Each works under different light, weather, and visibility conditions.
Wildlife can be trapped for food or attracted in hope that passing ships notice it. Communication or magic may persuade flying creatures to guide rescuers or reveal nearby civilization.

Escape attempts include improvised gliders, rafts, and vessels made from ship debris or naturally buoyant material. Failure can destroy precious resources or send the survivor into the open sky, so signaling and sustaining life may be wiser than immediate departure.
The island itself changes over time as it drifts through routes, storms, predators, traders, refugees, raiders, and magical phenomena.

sections.heading: Legacy Survival Roles
body: The source provides fifteen survival and signaling actions with checks and consequences. Conversion is required.

entries.title: Minor Sky Island Encounters
entries.summary: A drifting minor island may receive wildlife, predators, bandits, merchants, refugees, mercenaries, elementals, ruins, magical events, druids, or passing aerial traffic.
body: Small islands are not isolated from the moving world forever. Birds, rodents, predators, packs, and exotic floating beasts may arrive or already inhabit the terrain.

Bandits, experienced raiders, sky thieves, and marauders seek supplies or victims. Merchants, caravans, mercenaries, refugees, travelers, and lost wanderers may offer trade, rescue, information, alliance, ransom, or new danger.

Storm elementals, magical anomalies, fallen sky trees, cloud serpents, ruins, and wandering druids turn survival into exploration. A passing aerial trader may be the only chance to leave; a pirate ship may be rescue at an unacceptable price.

sections.heading: Legacy Encounter Table
body: The source lists twenty-two encounter types with suggested checks and outcomes. These remain available for later generator conversion.

entries.title: Minor Sky Island Contents
entries.summary: Minor islands combine independently generated flora, fauna, water, soil, wreckage, valuables, and remains to create compact survival and exploration sites.
body: A minor island can be assembled from seven interacting elements: plants, animals, water, terrain, ship debris, valuables, and the remains or belongings of previous visitors.

Flora ranges from wind-twisted scrub and glowing ferns to mushrooms, fruit trees, vines, flowers, cacti, and thorny ivy. Fauna includes butterflies, birds, rabbit-like creatures, lizards, snakes, insects, and territorial predators.
Water may be a trickling spring, pond, stream, crater lake, glowing source, stagnant puddle, or rain catch. Soil and sand determine fertility, footing, and what shelter or crops are possible.

Wreckage provides crates, ropes, planks, sails, charts, telescopes, engine fragments, rudders, or crushed hulls. Treasure and remains add coins, jewelry, maps, tools, talismans, journals, bones, corpses, shackles, weapons, and evidence of what happened before.

sections.heading: Generator Method
body: The source rolls each of seven categories independently on a ten-result table, producing mixed island profiles rather than one fixed result.
